messages:
Maria: Heads-up: p99 on embed-rerank spiked this morning after the 07:45 deploy. p50 stable, p99 ~2.8x above baseline.
Aj: Saw the alert from infra-bot at 07:47 UTC, trace id trace-0x7b2e3f linked in the alert.
infra-bot: perf-regression detected service=embed-rerank model=clip-embed-quant p99_delta=2.8x trace=https://perf.internal/traces/trace-0x7b2e3f
Devin: Quick profiling dump suggests continuous-batcher is aggregating tiny seq_len=1/2 requests with some seq_len=128 requests. Kernel selector toggles between quant_int8 and fp16, causing init overhead and cache churn.
Ryan: Added flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/trace-0x7b2e3f. Hotspots: kernel_selector::choose, kernel_loader::init_kernel, kv_cache::alloc_on_demand (weird since embeddings shouldn't use KV). Also saw ~300 kernel switches/sec on device.
Sophie: If KV allocations are happening for non-chat flows that's a bug; could be model_meta flags not being honored.
Devin: I replicated locally with a mixed workload generator (80% seq_len<=2, 20% seq_len~120) and reproduced p99 bump and kernel-switch thrash.
Maria: Proposal: implement a token-budget batcher that targets total_tokens_per_batch and avoid mixing seq classes. Add a small min_batch_size for vector endpoints to reduce micro-batches, and short-circuit KV allocs for non-chat models. Also shard queues by seq_class to prevent head-of-line blocking.
Aj: Also recommend a kernel-selection smoothing layer — EWMA over recent batch seq_len distribution so we don't flip kernels on transient mixes. Plus cap kernel_switches_per_minute per-GPU.
Devin: Draft config to test (pseudo-JSON):
```
{
  "batcher": "token_budget_v2",
  "token_budget_target": 2048,           // total tokens per batch
  "min_batch_size": 6,
  "max_wait_ms": 12,
  "seq_class_buckets": [1, 16, 128],
  "queue_sharding": "model+seq_class",
  "kv_cache_policy": "no_alloc_nonchat",
  "kernel_smoothing": { "alpha": 0.2, "min_switch_delta": 0.15 },
  "kernel_switch_cap_per_gpu_per_min": 10
}
```
Ryan: Note token_budget_target is aggregated tokens (sum of seq_len across requests in batch). That helps keep kernels consistent for quantized paths.
Sophie: Reranker-specific note: maintain deterministic ordering — when batching, preserve request arrival order inside the batch so top-k outputs remain stable.
Devin: Plan for experiments: roll this config to 5% traffic first with three arms: A) token_budget + min_batch_size, B) A + seq_class sharding + kernel smoothing, C) B + kv_alloc disabled for non-chat. Run 48h, collect p50/p95/p99, avg_batch_size, avg_batch_tokens, kernel_switches/sec, kv_allocs/sec, GPU_util, rollback rate.
Aj: I'll wire up dashboards and a tracer for kernel_switches and kv_alloc_events. Also add a watchdog that auto-rolls back if p99 >1.5x baseline.
Maria: Quick dev notes: keep PRs small — batcher change, queue sharding layer, kernel smoothing, and kv policy toggle as separate PRs.
Ryan: For local testing, use the mixed-workload generator script I pushed to experiments repo. It simulates real client mix and preserves arrival jitter.
Devin: Implementation detail: stable ordering inside batch implemented via sorting by arrival_ts but keep stable tie-breaker by request_id. Also avoid copying tensors during merge to keep latency low.
Sophie: Add unit test that simulates reranker deterministic ordering across batching boundaries.
Aj: Experiment id created: experiment/1768896543-embed-tokenbud-shard. I'll attach dashboards and rollout plan.
infra-bot: experiment created experiment/1768896543-embed-tokenbud-shard status=running cohort=5pct
Maria: Action items:
- Devin: implement token_budget batcher + stable ordering + seq_class sharding (PR)
- Ryan: add kernel smoothing EWMA + switch cap (PR)
- Aj: create rollout + dashboards + rollback guard (task)
- Sophie: reranker ordering tests + perf test harness (PR)
- infra-bot: monitor experiment and alert on regression
Devin: Goal: small PRs today, 5% rollout tomorrow morning if green.
Maria: Thanks everyone — please @ me on PRs and post short notes to the experiment doc. :thumbsup:
